mentions.name: Modbus plant watering controller
mentions.description: A standalone hardware device that automates watering plants by controlling water valves. The current version uses Modbus over RS485 so valve nodes can be daisy-chained: an ESP32 master node with cheap Puya PY32 MCU slave nodes, allowing more valves to be added without recompiling firmware or routing extra wires to a central control box. It is intentionally simple, with no Home Assistant or similar home automation stack.
mentions.problem: The first version was a central box controlling all valves, which required routing every wire into it (at least two for power) — the bigger the garden, the more wires needed. The author also wanted a simple standalone device after being bitten in the past by more complex setups.
mentions.audience: The author's own plant/garden watering; a deliberately simple standalone device with no Home Assistant or similar platform involved.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Working on a simple device that can automate watering my plant.

The first version is just simple box that controlling a bunch of valves to control waterflow, quickly learn my mistake that i have to route every wires into that box(at least 2 for power), the bigger your garden, the more wires you use.

Now the current version use Modbus over RS485 so that i can daisy chain the valves, and can extend more valves without compiling new FW.

The master node uses esp32 and the slave node uses the cheapest mcu i can find(Puya py32)

Sometimes i just want a simple device like that, no home assistant or anything, have been bitten in the past.
